A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RaBiT research. All 27 pages of each version, including Appendices A–J, provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, algorithms, and kernel listings supporting reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original quantization accuracy, component ablations, training-dynamics analyses, initialization experiments, and inference measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds residual-alignment comparisons, comparative training times, and seed and optimizer stability results.

M1.justification: The shared-weight residual derivation, learnable scales, surrogate gradients, training objective, and two-stage initialization remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 and the appendix kernel code are identical; the AdamW experiment tests the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions use WikiText-2/C4 and the same commonsense, reasoning, and instruction-following benchmarks. The added analyses use existing Llama2-7B coverage and introduce no new datasets, domains, or task scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds DB-LLM and MBOK to the previously Standard-QAT-versus-RaBiT decomposition comparison. New Table 11 compares training time against Single-Path INT2 QAT and Standard Independent QAT. The main accuracy and inference comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds residual alignment as a diagnostic metric, an AdamW-versus-Muon evaluation, and a per-epoch training-time comparison. Existing training budgets and benchmark protocols remain unchanged. Table 6's warm-up description is newly disclosed information, not evidence of a changed timing procedure.

E4.justification: Expanded Table 1 tests whether path anticorrelation corresponds to functional residual correction across additional methods. New Appendix F.4 examines sensitivity to random seeds and optimizer choice. Existing component, initialization, convergence, and layer-wise analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V1 provides no seed-variability reporting. V2 Table 13 reports five specified seeds, individual outcomes, means, and standard deviations for Llama2-7B perplexity and QA accuracy. This addition is confined to one model; no formal test supports the accompanying claim of statistical identity between optimizers.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds comparator and residual-alignment results and changes several amplitude/covariance values, including Standard QAT's layer-15 amplitude from 0.0214 to 0.0213. New results include comparative training times, five-seed QA accuracy of 61.57% with SD 0.23, and AdamW perplexity of 5.78. Main benchmark and decoding scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Equation 2 explicitly decomposes MSE using the functional residual R1 = yt − y1 and its correlation with the second path, supporting the distinction between residual alignment and path anticorrelation. Related residual reasoning already existed in the appendices; their propositions and proofs are unchanged apart from equation numbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about inter-path adaptation, residual coupling, initialization, competitive 2-bit accuracy, memory savings, and 4.49× inference speed-up.

C2.justification: Section 3 now explicitly states that negative path correlation alone is insufficient and interprets residual alignment as stronger evidence of error correction. Section 5.2 narrows its VQ comparison from resolving the historical trade-off to narrowing the accuracy gap. Table 6 qualifies kernel timings as warm-cache measurements.

D1.justification: V2 discloses approximately 2.02 effective bits including scale storage, clarifies warm-up/cache conditions for kernel timings, and adds comparative per-epoch training costs on four H100s. Existing hyperparameters, pseudocode, kernel implementation, and access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4.3 adds Molchanov et al. (2019) and Martens and Grosse (2015), connecting preconditioning to Fisher-based and K-FAC-style sensitivity intuition. Section 3 also sharpens the mechanistic comparison with DB-LLM and MBOK; the broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: V2 locally rewrites the motivation and VQ discussion, expands the preconditioning explanation, adds Appendix F.4 and acknowledgments, and replaces the preprint notice with conference publication text. The overall section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains comparator rows and a residual-alignment column and reorders its columns. V2 adds Tables 11 and 13, renumbers the retained grid-search table to 12, expands Table 6's caption, and resizes or relocates some displays. The six figures retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the evidence with a more discriminating residual-alignment comparison and seed/optimizer checks, while clarifying storage overhead, timing conditions, and training costs. These improve interpretation and transparency without changing the main results. The gains remain limited: stability checks cover Llama2-7B, and the existing theoretical guarantees are not strengthened.
